activities.title: Secant lines close in on the tangent
Stationary is not always max or min

assessmentPoints: Secant-gradient answers in the opening activity
Worksheet and exit-ticket answers in the fifth activity
successCriteria: Secant lines close in on the tangent - a secant gives an average gradient between two points; slide the points together and the secant becomes the tangent, whose gradient is dy/dx.
objectives.text: Explain dy/dx as the gradient of the tangent, the limit of secant gradients

assessmentPoints: Power-rule answers in the second activity
First-principles answers in the third activity
Worksheet and exit-ticket answers in the fifth activity
successCriteria: The power rule - differentiate term by term: bring the power down and reduce it by one, so x^3 becomes 3x^2 and x^5 becomes 5x^4, while a constant becomes 0.
dy/dx from first principles - the secant gradient (f(x + h) - f(x)) / h for y = x^2 simplifies to 2x + h, and letting h tend to 0 gives the exact gradient 2x.
objectives.text: Use the power rule and first principles to differentiate polynomials

assessmentPoints: Stationary-point answers in the fourth activity
Trap answers in the fifth activity
Worksheet and exit-ticket answers in the fifth activity
successCriteria: Stationary points: max, min, inflexion - solve dy/dx = 0, then read the sign change of dy/dx either side: positive to negative is a maximum, negative to positive a minimum, no change an inflexion.
Stationary is not always max or min - for y = x^3 the gradient reaches 0 at x = 0 yet stays positive on both sides, so the curve climbs through a point of inflexion.
objectives.text: Find stationary points from dy/dx = 0 and classify them with the sign-change test
